Configuration restore

Apply a saved configuration back to a FortiWeb — from the vault or an uploaded .conf — with a dry run first, a mandatory pre-restore backup and a typed confirmation. Administrator only.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage backups.restore
📍 WhereAppliances → (device) → Appliance Actions → Restore (URL /appliances/<id>/restore)

What is it?#

Restore uploads a saved configuration to a FortiWeb, which applies it and reboots. The page also manages the appliance's configuration vault: list, upload, pull from the device, download and delete. Because a live restore replaces the whole running configuration and interrupts every service the device fronts, the page is administrator-only, validates by default (dry run), takes a backup first (and stops if it cannot) and asks you to type the appliance name.

What does it do?#

  • Backup vault card: the appliance's stored backups (file, source, size, time, enc badge), Download and Delete, an upload form (Upload a config backup (.conf) from your PC → Add) and Pull backup from device.
  • Restore now card: pick a stored backup (Restore from a stored backup) or upload a file to restore directly (…or upload a .conf to restore directly), give the backup password if the file is encrypted, and Validate / Restore.
  • A dry run checks the file and shows what would be sent, without contacting the device.
  • A live run first stores a pre-restore backup of the current configuration in the vault (pulled over the device REST API), then uploads the selected file to the device. If the pre-restore backup cannot be taken, the live run is aborted unless you explicitly chose to restore without one.
  • On FortiADC the vault works (pull over SSH, upload, download), but applying a backup is not possible from SATOM: FortiADC has no REST restore endpoint. The page says so and tells you to restore from the FortiADC GUI (System > Settings > Restore) or CLI (execute restore config).

Requirements#

  • A FortiWeb (or FortiADC, for the vault only).
  • On a multi-ADOM FortiWeb, the row that owns the device. A backup contains every ADOM, so restoring it restores all of them. Other ADOM rows are redirected to the owning row.
  • For an encrypted backup, its backup password.

Permissions#

Every route of this page requires users.manage and backups.restore — in the seeded profiles, an administrator. Either permission alone is not enough.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the page now also requires backups.restore, and a live restore is aborted when the pre-restore backup cannot be taken, unless you tick Restore without a pre-restore backup.

🔑Permission — Without the permission

The Restore button is not shown on the appliance page, and the restore URLs answer 403 Forbidden. Operators manage the vault from Device backups instead.

How to use#

Validate a restore (dry run)#

  1. Open the appliance's page and click Restore under Appliance Actions.
  2. In Restore now, choose a backup in Restore from a stored backup, or choose a file under …or upload a .conf to restore directly.
  3. If the file is encrypted, enter Backup password (only if the backup is encrypted).
  4. Leave Dry run (validate only — nothing is sent to the appliance) ticked and click Validate / Restore.
  5. The Result — DRY RUN card shows DRY-RUN — would upload fweb-01.conf (812,345 bytes) to the appliance and reboot. No file was sent., the file, whether it is encrypted, and the device endpoint that would receive it.

Restore for real#

  1. Untick Dry run. A red box appears: A live restore reboots fweb-01 and replaces its configuration. A pre-restore backup is pulled over REST first; if that fails the restore is aborted.
  2. Leave Restore without a pre-restore backup unticked (see below).
  3. Type the appliance name in Type the appliance name fweb-01 to authorise:.
  4. Click Validate / Restore.
  5. SATOM pulls a backup of the current configuration into the vault over REST, then uploads the selected file. The Result — LIVE RESTORE card shows restore uploaded to the appliance (HTTP 200) — it is applying the configuration and may reboot. and the name of the Pre-restore backup.

A file uploaded on the Restore card is also kept in the vault.

When the pre-restore backup cannot be taken#

The pre-restore backup is pulled over the device REST API only. If that fails (for example because REST backups are refused by a backup password), the live restore is aborted and nothing is sent: Live restore aborted: the pre-restore backup could not be taken (…). Nothing was sent to fweb-01.

  1. Take a backup from Device backups over SSH, so the vault holds a rollback copy.
  2. Back on Restore, untick Dry run, tick Restore without a pre-restore backup (Only if the device REST backup cannot work (e.g. a backup password is set). There is then no rollback copy; the choice is recorded in the audit log.), type the name and click Validate / Restore.
  3. The result shows Pre-restore backup (none: RuntimeError; restored without a pre-restore backup).

Manage the vault from this page#

  • Add stores an uploaded .conf (Stored "fweb-01.conf" in the vault (812.4 KB).).
  • Pull backup from device asks the device for a backup (REST first, SSH fallback) and stores it: Pulled "fweb-01_20261003_101500_cli.conf" from fweb-01 into the vault.
  • The download and trash icons work as on Device backups.

Field Description Required Example

…or upload a .conf to restore directly A file from your computer (.conf, .zip, .gz offered); takes precedence over the selection One of the two —
Backup password Only for encrypted backups No —
Dry run Validate only; ticked by default — ticked
Type the appliance name Required for a live restore Live only fweb-01

Example#

🧪Example — Rolling back a bad change

An operator changed many policies on fweb-01 this morning and the site broke.

  1. An administrator opens Restore on fweb-01 and picks last night's backup.
  2. Dry run: the result confirms the file and endpoint.
  3. Live run with the typed name. The pre-restore backup keeps this morning's configuration in the vault, in case it is needed for analysis.
  4. After the reboot, run a Rediscovery so SATOM's cache reflects the restored configuration.

Result#

  • A live run writes the audit entry appliance.restore with the file, the pre-restore backup, whether it ran without one, and the outcome. A run aborted because the pre-restore backup failed is recorded with the outcome refused. Uploads, pulls and deletions write appliance.backup_upload, appliance.backup_fetch and appliance.backup_delete.
  • The device applies the configuration and may reboot. SATOM's cache is not refreshed automatically; run a Rediscovery afterwards.
  • Actions on this page run as jobs (Restore configuration, Upload configuration backup, Fetch configuration backup). See Jobs.

Troubleshooting#

"Live restore aborted: the pre-restore backup could not be taken (…)"#

Possible causes — The device REST backup failed: a backup password is set, the licence is invalid, or REST is unreachable.

Solution — Store an SSH backup from Device backups first, then restore with Restore without a pre-restore backup ticked. See When the pre-restore backup cannot be taken.

Verification — The result card shows Result — LIVE RESTORE.

"Live restore requires typing the exact appliance name to confirm."#

Solution — Type the name exactly as in the page title, including case.

"Choose a stored backup or upload a .conf file to restore."#

Solution — Select a vault entry or choose a file.

"Stored backup unreadable: …"#

Possible causes — The file is missing on disk, or its checksum no longer matches (sha256 mismatch … — refusing to use).

Solution — Use another backup.

"Cannot connect to fweb-01: …"#

Possible causes — The device is unreachable or the credentials fail.

Solution — Run Test Connection on the appliance page and fix the connection first.

"restore upload failed (HTTP 4xx)."#

Possible causes — The device rejected the file: wrong product or firmware, or an encrypted file without the correct password.

Solution — Check the backup's firmware against the device's current firmware (shown as Current firmware: on the page) and the password.

"Could not fetch a backup from fweb-01: … You can upload a .conf manually instead."#

Possible causes — Both the REST backup and the SSH fallback failed.

Solution — See Device backups.

Advanced#

Advanced What is sent

The file is uploaded as a multipart request to the device's configuration-restore endpoint, resolved from the endpoint registry for the device's firmware, with a 10-minute timeout. The backup password, when given, is sent with it.
